page: Amazon Web Services c7a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring 16 dedicated physical cores powered by 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9R14 processors on the x86_64 architecture. With one hardware thread per core, the system provides dedicated compute slices devoid of simultaneous multithreading resource contention. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 clocked at 5 GHz, maintaining a 2 GB per core ratio characteristic of compute-bound architectures. Instruction set capabilities include AVX-512 extensions with VNNI and bfloat16, cryptographic acceleration through AES and SHA-NI, and a 32 MB L3 cache.

The server does not include bundled local instance storage, requiring persistent storage needs to be addressed through external network-attached volumes. Networking provides a baseline throughput of 6 Gbps, and no discrete GPUs are present. Benchmark results demonstrate upper-quartile single-core performance on stress-ng evaluations, alongside strong execution rates for lightweight language model token generation using AVX-512 vectorized paths. Memory bandwidth reaches 62.26 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 47.81 GB/sec for writes, delivering balanced throughput across mid-range data operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7a.4xlarge provides a high density of physical AMD compute cores relative to its memory footprint, avoiding unnecessary memory overhead for calculation-centric workloads. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage and a modest 32 GB RAM allocation, which limits suitability for large in-memory databases. The instance profile aligns closely with continuous integration and build pipelines, software compilation via toolchains like Clang, static web serving fleets, media transcoding, and distributed worker nodes for batch analytics.
description: Amazon Web Services c7a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 16 dedicated physical cores running at 3.7 GHz with one thread per core, paired with 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 system memory at a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio. The instance includes modern vector execution instructions such as AVX-512 with VNNI and bfloat16 support, alongside 32 MB of L3 cache. It provides a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps and does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring persistent storage to be attached externally. Benchmark metrics show strong single-core compute performance and fast execution on lightweight language model inference, backed by steady multi-core processing throughput. The c7a.4xlarge provides an efficient compute-dense platform suited for batch processing, CI/CD pipelines, software compilation, video encoding, and distributed compute worker nodes.
